original_interpretation: The September 2024 worldwide NS and RS licence requirements (742.4(a)(5), 742.6(a)(10)) use a presumption of approval for Country Group A:1 destinations and a presumption of denial for D:1 or D:5 destinations.
evidence_found: Preamble: "...license review policy for the items in paragraph (a)(5), which is a presumption of approval when the export or reexport is to a country in Country Group A:1 ... For exports or reexports of such items to destinations specified in Country Group D:1 or D:5, license applications will be reviewed with a presumption of denial." Regulatory text, new 742.4(b)(10): "License applications to export or reexport items described in paragraph (a)(5)(i) of this section to destinations specified in Country Group A:1, A:5, and A:6 ... will be reviewed with a presumption of approval. ... Country Groups D:1 or D:5 ... will be reviewed under a presumption of denial." Same wording for 742.6(b)(11) / (a)(10). (89 FR 72926, sec. III.E and amendatory text). Current eCFR 742.4(b)(10) (2026-09-01) reads the same (A:1, A:5, A:6).
correction: The operative regulatory text (742.4(b)(10) and 742.6(b)(11)) gives a presumption of approval for Country Groups A:1, A:5 and A:6, not A:1 only; only the preamble summary says A:1. Other destinations are case-by-case.
notes: The claim follows the preamble; the amendatory text and current eCFR are broader.

original_interpretation: The companion December 2024 Entity List rule (89 FR 96830, effective 2 December 2024) added 140 entities under China, Japan, South Korea and Singapore, modified 14 Chinese entries, gave nine new and seven modified entries the entity-specific foreign-produced item (FN5) designation, and removed three entities from the VEU program.
evidence_found: "adding 140 entities to the Entity List. These entries are listed on the Entity List under the destinations of China, People's Republic of (China), Japan, South Korea, and Singapore ... This final rule also modifies 14 existing entries on the Entity List, consisting of revisions to 14 entries under China ... designates nine of these entities being added and seven of the entries being modified as entities for which entity-specific restrictions involving foreign-produced items apply. This final rule also amends the EAR by removing three entities from the Validated End- User (VEU) Program." (89 FR 96830 abstract; FR API record 2024-28267, effective_on 2024-12-02, published 2024-12-05)
notes: Abstract says 'entity-specific restrictions involving foreign-produced items'; the FN5 label is the researcher's (consistent with 89 FR 96790). Published 5 Dec 2024.

original_interpretation: The December 2024 rule replaced the '18 nm half-pitch or less' DRAM criterion in the advanced-node IC definition with a memory cell area below 0.0019 square micrometres or a memory density above 0.288 gigabits per square millimetre, because the old test missed denser cell designs, 3D-stacked DRAM and HBM.
evidence_found: "this IFR removes the criterion using a ``production'' `technology node' of `18 nanometer half pitch or less' and adds in its place two different criteria ... a memory cell area of less than 0.0019 square micrometers ([mu]m2); or a memory density greater than 0.288 gigabits per square mm." and "that definition allowed fabrication facilities to make substantial improvements in memory density by using more compact memory cell architectures, as well as by stacking DRAM in three dimensions, without meeting the definition, thereby avoiding controls. Furthermore, the previous definition did not capture HBM" (89 FR 96790, preamble sec. III.B.4, revisions to definition of advanced-node IC)

original_interpretation: The December 2024 rule added eight new red flags, (b)(20) through (b)(27), to BIS's Know Your Customer guidance in Supplement No. 3 to Part 732.
evidence_found: "In supplement no. 3 to part 732 (BIS's ``Know Your Customer'' Guidance and Red Flags), this IFR adds eight new Red Flags under paragraphs (b)(20) through (27)" (89 FR 96790, preamble, 'Addition of Eight New Red Flags To Assist With Compliance')
notes: Preamble adds these are in addition to five red flags added by the October 2023 AC/S IFR.

original_interpretation: Under 15 CFR 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(B), foreign-produced SME that is subject to the EAR only through the SME de minimis rule or the SME FDP rule is excluded from the licence requirement when exported from abroad by an entity located in a Supplement No. 4 country that is not headquartered, and whose ultimate parent is not headquartered, in Macau or a Country Group D:5 destination.
evidence_found: "(B) An item subject to the EAR pursuant to § 734.4(a)(8) or § 734.9(k) if the item is reexported or exported from abroad by an entity located in a country specified in supplement no. 4 to this part, and the entity is not headquartered or have an ultimate parent company headquartered in either Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5." (15 CFR 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(B), eCFR as of 2026-09-01)
notes: 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(C) adds a parallel exclusion for entities in any country that has implemented equivalent controls (not only Supplement No. 4 countries).

original_interpretation: Under the EAR's general de minimis rules (15 CFR 734.4), foreign-made items with controlled US content above 10% of value are subject to the EAR when reexported to Country Group E:1/E:2 destinations, and above 25% for other destinations.
evidence_found: "(c) 10% De Minimis Rule ... the following reexports are not subject to the EAR when made to any country in the world ... (1) Reexports of a foreign-made commodity incorporating controlled U.S.-origin commodities ... valued at 10% or less of the total value"; "(d) 25% De Minimis Rule ... not subject to the EAR when made to countries other than those listed in Country Group E:1 or E:2 ... valued at 25% or less" (15 CFR 734.4(c)-(d), eCFR 2026-09-01)
notes: Subject to the no-de-minimis exceptions in 734.4(a) and the conditions in 734.4(b).

original_interpretation: There is no de minimis level under the SME FDP rule for foreign tools meeting ECCN 3B001.a.4, c, d, f.1, f.5, f.6, k to n, p.2, p.4, r or 3B002.c: any US-origin IC content makes them subject to the EAR for Macau and Country Group D:5.
evidence_found: "(8) There is no de minimis level related to the SME FDP rule for a commodity meeting the parameters in ECCNs 3B001.a.4, c, d, f.1, f.5, f.6, k to n, p.2, p.4, r, or 3B002.c ... when the commodity contains a U.S.-origin integrated circuit specified under Category 3, 4, or 5 of the CCL, and the commodity is destined for Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5, unless excluded from the national security license requirement in § 742.4(a)(4) or the regional stability license requirement in § 742.6(a)(6) of the EAR." (15 CFR 734.4(a)(8), eCFR 2026-09-01)
correction: Not 'any US-origin IC content': the tool must contain a US-origin IC specified under CCL Category 3, 4 or 5 (i.e. a listed, not EAR99, IC), and the rule does not apply where the export is excluded from the licence requirement under 742.4(a)(4) or 742.6(a)(6) (e.g. exports by Supplement No. 4 country entities).
notes: SRC-0284 (press release) not re-checked for this claim; the regulatory text is the authority.

original_interpretation: As of September 2026, 15 CFR 734.9 contains FDP rules for national security items, 9x515, 600 series, Entity List footnotes 1, 4 and 5, Russia/Belarus/Crimea, Russia/Belarus military end users, advanced computing, supercomputers, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and AI model weights.
evidence_found: eCFR 15 CFR 734.9 (2026-09-01) paragraph headings: "(b) National Security FDP rule"; "(c) 9x515 FDP rule"; "(d) '600 series' FDP rule"; "(e) Entity List FDP rules" (Footnote 1, Footnote 4, 'footnote 5 and advanced-node integrated Circuit Production'); "(f) Russia/Belarus/Temporarily occupied Crimea region of Ukraine FDP rule"; "(g) Russia/Belarus-Military End User and Procurement FDP rule"; "(h) Advanced computing FDP rule"; "(i) 'Supercomputer' FDP rule"; "(j) Iran FDP rule"; "(k) Semiconductor Manufacturing Equipment (SME) FDP rule"; "(l) AI Model weights FDP rule"
correction: The list omits paragraph (j), the Iran FDP rule; 734.9 as of 2026-09-01 contains 11 FDP rules in (b)-(l), including Iran.
notes: The AI model weights FDP rule (l) is still in the eCFR text as of 2026-09-01, consistent with the AI Diffusion rule not having been formally removed.

original_interpretation: The advanced computing FDP rule (734.9(h)) can reach foreign-produced items destined to any location worldwide when its product and destination scope conditions are met, while the SME FDP rule (734.9(k)) applies when there is knowledge the item is destined to Macau or a Country Group D:5 destination.
evidence_found: "(2) Destination or end use scope of the advanced computing FDP rule. A foreign-produced item meets the destination scope of this paragraph (h)(2) if there is 'knowledge' that the foreign-produced item is: (i) Destined to any location worldwide or will be incorporated into any 'part,' 'component,' 'computer,' or 'equipment' not designated EAR99 destined to any location worldwide; or (ii) 'Technology' 'developed' by an entity headquartered in ... Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5"; "(2) Destination scope of the SME FDP rule ... if there is 'knowledge' that the foreign-produced item is destined to Macau or a destination in Country Group D:5" (15 CFR 734.9(h)(2), (k)(2), eCFR 2026-09-01)
notes: Licence requirements for (h) items are set in 742.6(a)(6); worldwide destination scope does not mean a worldwide licence requirement.

original_interpretation: The AI Diffusion interim final rule is 90 FR 4544, published 15 January 2025 (effective 13 January 2025); it revised advanced computing IC controls and added a control on certain closed-weight AI model weights.
evidence_found: FR API record 2025-00636: citation "90 FR 4544", publication_date "2025-01-15", effective_on "2025-01-13"; abstract: "BIS revises the Export Administration Regulations' (EAR) controls on advanced computing integrated circuits (ICs) and adds a new control on artificial intelligence (AI) model weights for certain advanced closed-weight dual-use AI models."
notes: 'AI Diffusion' is the common name, not in the abstract (the abstract refers to 'responsible diffusion').

original_interpretation: The Entity List affiliates rule is 90 FR 47201, 'Expansion of End-User Controls To Cover Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities', published 30 September 2025 and effective 29 September 2025.
evidence_found: FR API record 2025-19001: citation "90 FR 47201", publication_date "2025-09-30", effective_on "2025-09-29"; abstract: "In this interim final rule (IFR), the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to address diversion concerns involving entities on the Entity List ... any entity that is at least 50 percent owned by one or more entities on the Entity List will itself automatically be subject to Entity List restrictions."
notes: Title not in the fetched fields; citation, dates and subject match. The API record for 90 FR 56001 (2025-22137, 5 Dec 2025) in the same source has no abstract; its relation to the affiliates rule was not checked.

original_interpretation: BIS Entity List rules in 2025 included 70 additions (90 FR 14032) and 12 additions (90 FR 14046) on 28 March 2025, and 32 additions (90 FR 44496) on 16 September 2025.
evidence_found: FR API abstracts: 90 FR 14032 (pub. 2025-03-28) "adding 70 entities to the Entity List"; 90 FR 14046 (pub. 2025-03-28, effective 2025-03-25) "adding 12 entities to the Entity List"; 90 FR 44496 (pub. 2025-09-16, effective 2025-09-12) "adding 32 entities to the Entity List"
notes: Dates are publication dates; 90 FR 44496 was published 16 Sep 2025 (effective 12 Sep). Destinations include China, Pakistan, Iran, UAE, South Africa, Taiwan, India, Singapore, Turkey.

original_interpretation: On 24 August 2026 (effective 21 August 2026) BIS removed two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List entries under China.
evidence_found: FR API record 2026-17231: citation "91 FR 54658", publication_date "2026-08-24", effective_on "2026-08-21"; abstract: "BIS revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China"
notes: Abstract adds that Arrow China Electronics Trading and six aliases were removed in November 2025.

original_interpretation: Inference: because South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Israel are not in Supplement No. 4 to Part 742, SME made there that falls under the SME FDP or SME de minimis rule needs a US licence for China, whereas the same tools made by Japanese or Dutch firms do not (they fall under national Japanese/Dutch controls instead).
evidence_found: Supplement No. 4 to Part 742 (eCFR 2026-09-01) lists: "Australia Austria Belgium Bulgaria Canada Croatia Czech Republic Denmark Estonia Finland France Germany Greece Hungary Iceland Ireland Italy Japan Latvia Lithuania Luxembourg Netherlands New Zealand Norway Poland Portugal Romania Slovakia Slovenia Spain Sweden Switzerland United Kingdom". 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(C): "An item subject to the EAR pursuant to § 734.4(a)(8) or § 734.9(k) if the item is reexported or exported from abroad by an entity located in a country that has implemented equivalent controls for items specified in paragraph (a)(4)(i) of this section, and the entity is not headquartered or have an ultimate parent company headquartered in either Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5."
correction: South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Israel are indeed absent from Supplement No. 4, but the inference omits the separate exclusion in 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(C) for exporters located in any country that has implemented equivalent controls; the licence need for such tools therefore depends on whether that country has equivalent controls, not only on Supplement No. 4 membership. The exclusion also turns on where the exporting entity is located and headquartered, not on the maker's nationality ('Japanese or Dutch firms'), and applies only to items subject to the EAR solely via 734.4(a)(8) or 734.9(k).
notes: Inference; checked against 742.4 and Supplement No. 4 (existing CLM-0860).

original_interpretation: A law-firm review dated August 2026 states that the AI Diffusion Rule was informally rescinded on 13 May 2025 but had still not been formally removed from the Code of Federal Regulations.
evidence_found: "In light of the controversy generated by the AI Diffusion Rule, on May 13, 2025, BIS announced that it was rescinding the rule and planned to issue a replacement in the future." "However, as of this writing, the AI Diffusion Rule has yet to be formally rescinded via an update to the Code of Federal Regulations." "BIS reminded exporters in May 2026 that the informal rescission left the pre-existing regulations in place" (Miller & Chevalier, 12 Aug 2026)
notes: Consistent with eCFR 734.9(l) 'AI Model weights FDP rule' still present as of 2026-09-01. Source type 'other' for a law-firm publication is acceptable (tier 3).

original_interpretation: Miller & Chevalier counts 143 Entity List additions in 2025 (82 in March, 32 in September, 29 in October) and none in the first half of 2026.
evidence_found: Miller & Chevalier (12 Aug 2026): "BIS added 82 entities to the Entity List" (March 2025), "32 more" (September), "29 in October"; "An unusually quiet first half of 2026 saw no additions or removals."
notes: 143 is the sum 82+32+29; the page excerpt did not show '143' stated as a total. The March 82 matches 70+12 in 90 FR 14032/14046 and September 32 matches 90 FR 44496. The FR API list of 2026 BIS rules shows the first 2026 Entity List rules on 24 Aug 2026 (91 FR 54657/54658, both removals), consistent with no H1 2026 changes.

original_interpretation: The BIS rules published from January to September 2026 that bear on semiconductors are the H200-class licence-policy revision (91 FR 1684, 15 Jan), the extension of approved/authorised IC designer deadlines (91 FR 17851, 9 Apr), UAE's move to Country Group A:5 with licence-free access to advanced computing items (91 FR 43034, 14 Jul), Entity List revisions for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) (91 FR 54658, 24 Aug) and a polysilicon anti-stockpiling rule (91 FR 60505, 24 Sep); no new SME or chip control-list rule was published.
evidence_found: Federal Register API (BIS rules, 2026-01-01 onward, count 12): includes "91 FR 1684 ... Revision to License Review Policy for Advanced Computing Commodities" (abstract: "changing it from a presumption of denial to a case-by-case review. The semiconductors covered by this rule are the Nvidia H200 and its equivalents"), 91 FR 17851, 91 FR 43034, 91 FR 54658, 91 FR 60505, and also "91 FR 5091 ... Conforming Change to the Export Administration Regulations for Cambodia" (abstract: "to reflect that Cambodia is no longer a Country Group D:5 country"), "91 FR 50701 DPAS Directive Allocation Order ... Recoverable Critical Minerals and Materials", 91 FR 54657 (one Turkey Entity List removal), and drone and firearms rules.
correction: The five listed rules are correctly identified and no new SME or chip control-list (CCL) rule appears among the 12 BIS rules, but the list omits 91 FR 5091 (4 Feb 2026), which removed Cambodia from Country Group D:5 and so narrows the destination scope of every D:5-based semiconductor control (SME FDP, advanced computing, 742.4(a)(4)). 91 FR 50701 (critical-minerals DPAS order on black mass and tungsten scrap) is arguably tangential.
notes: Inference; the FR list covers type RULE only and was pulled 2026-09-30.

original_interpretation: Effective 10 July 2026, BIS moved the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 to A:5 and gave the UAE government and approved UAE commercial entities licence-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 US-UAE AI cooperation framework.
evidence_found: FR API record 2026-14132: citation "91 FR 43034", published 2026-07-14, "This rule is effective July 10, 2026."; abstract: "BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5 ... The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework"

original_interpretation: A BIS temporary final rule effective 22 September to 3 December 2026 (91 FR 60505) sets criteria to stop companies stockpiling polysilicon and derivatives before Section 232 import adjustments under Proclamation 11052 take effect on 4 December 2026.
evidence_found: FR API record 2026-19537 (91 FR 60505, published 2026-09-24): "This rule is effective September 22, 2026, through December 3, 2026."; abstract: "On August 6, 2026, the President issued Proclamation 11052 ... ordering the Secretary of Commerce (Secretary) to take action to restrict imports by a company if he determines the company is stockpiling polysilicon or polysilicon derivatives (Polysilicon Products) in advance of import adjustments that will be effective on December 4, 2026."
notes: The mechanism is an import prohibition on companies found stockpiling, plus import limits on new importers registering on or after 6 Aug 2026. The abstract does not use the words 'Section 232'; Proclamation title 'Adjusting Imports' is the Section 232 form, but that label was not confirmed in the fetched text.

original_interpretation: BIS removed Intel Semiconductor (Dalian), Samsung China Semiconductor and SK hynix Semiconductor (China) from the Validated End-User list for China by a rule published 2 September 2025 (90 FR 42321), effective 31 December 2025.
evidence_found: FR API record 2025-16735: citation "90 FR 42321", publication_date 2025-09-02, "This rule is effective December 31, 2025."; abstract: "revise the existing Validated End-User (VEU) Authorizations list for the People's Republic of China (PRC) by removing Intel Semiconductor (Dalian) Ltd; Samsung China Semiconductor Co. Ltd; and SK hynix Semiconductor (China) Ltd."
notes: Follow-on: SK hynix's 2026 prospectus says BIS granted it an annual licence for 2026 in December 2025 (new claim in this batch).

original_interpretation: VEU authorisation let approved end users receive eligible commodities, software and technology without their suppliers needing an individual BIS export, reexport or transfer licence.
evidence_found: "Pursuant to Sec. 748.15, VEU-eligible destinations may obtain eligible items without the need for the VEU's supplier to obtain an export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) license from the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). VEU-eligible items vary among VEUs and may include commodities, software, and/or technology, apart from items controlled for missile technology or crime control reasons" (90 FR 42321, I. Background)
notes: Excludes MT- and CC-controlled items.

original_interpretation: BIS estimated that removing the three China fabs from the VEU program would generate about 1,000 additional licence applications a year.
evidence_found: "BIS estimates that these new removal of these entities from the VEU program under the EAR will result in the submission of an additional 1,000 license applications annually, which would be an increase of 495 burden hours." (90 FR 42321, Rulemaking Requirements para. 2)
notes: Paperwork Reduction Act estimate made before implementation. ArentFox Schiff notes it excludes applications from TSMC's Nanjing site. In practice BIS moved to annual licences (SK hynix reports a 2026 annual licence granted Dec 2025), so actual application counts may differ.

original_interpretation: BIS said it intends to grant licences allowing former VEU participants to operate their existing fabs in China, but not licences to expand capacity or upgrade technology there, and gave them 120 days after publication to obtain licences.
evidence_found: "Former VEU participants will have 120 days following publication of the rule in the Federal Register to apply for and obtain export licenses. Going forward, BIS intends to grant export license applications to allow former VEU participants to operate their existing fabs in China. However, BIS does not intend to grant licenses to expand capacity or upgrade technology at fabs in China." (BIS press release, 29 Aug 2025)
notes: Substance verified; the researcher's quote 'BIS does intend to grant' is not verbatim (the release says 'Going forward, BIS intends to grant'). 120 days after 2 Sep 2025 publication is the 31 Dec 2025 effective date.

original_interpretation: A law-firm alert reported that TSMC's Nanjing site was also notified that its VEU authorisation would be revoked, and that the Intel Dalian facility had been acquired by SK hynix.
evidence_found: "Although not named in the announcement, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) also announced that its Nanjing site will lose its VEU designation on the same date."; "SK hynix acquired Intel's Dalian facility earlier this year." (ArentFox Schiff alert, 15 Sep 2025)
notes: The alert attributes the Nanjing news to a TSMC announcement ('TSMC also announced'), not to a BIS notice; the claim's 'was notified' is compatible but the primary source would be TSMC's statement (not checked). ArentFox Schiff source_type 'other' is acceptable.

original_interpretation: Reuters reported in July 2024, citing two unnamed sources, that the planned expansion of the FDP rule would exclude shipments from Japan, the Netherlands and South Korea, and over 30 other A:5 countries.
evidence_found: "But shipments from allies that export key chipmaking equipment - including Japan, the Netherlands and South Korea - will be excluded"; "Aside from Japan, the Netherlands and South Korea, the draft rule exempts over 30 other countries which are part of the same A:5 group."; "... two sources familiar with the rule said." (Reuters via RTE, 31 Jul 2024)
notes: Accurately records a report on a draft. The final rule (Supplement No. 4 to Part 742) did not exclude South Korea; this is already recorded as CON-0025 (CLM-0904 vs CLM-0860).

original_interpretation: Interpretation: the US semiconductor export-control regime works through five stacked layers: (1) item controls by ECCN and threshold (3A090, 4A090, 3B001/3B090/3B993, 3D/3E); (2) end-use controls on advanced fabs and supercomputers (744.23); (3) end-user controls via the Entity List and VEU; (4) extraterritorial reach via FDP and de minimis rules; and (5) controls on US persons' activities (744.6).
evidence_found: Structure checked against the regulatory text: item controls (ECCNs incl. 3B993 added/revised by 89 FR 96790); FDP rules in 15 CFR 734.9(b)-(l) and de minimis in 734.4; end-use controls in 744.23; 'U.S. person' support controls referenced in 89 FR 96790 as defined in Sec. 744.6; Entity List and VEU (90 FR 42321).
notes: Reasonable interpretation. Caveat: VEU is an authorisation (a relaxation) rather than a control; the licence exceptions and carve-outs (Supplement No. 4, equivalent-controls exclusion, RFF, HBM) are a cross-cutting sixth element not named.

original_interpretation: Interpretation: the regime evolved from company-specific measures (Huawei 2019-20, SMIC 2020) to country-wide technology thresholds for China (October 2022), then to anti-circumvention refinements (October 2023 performance density, 40+ countries), then to FDP rules reaching foreign tools and HBM (December 2024) and supply-chain due diligence on foundries and OSATs (January 2025); 2025-26 changes mostly adjusted licensing and end-user lists rather than adding new item controls.
evidence_found: FR records checked: 89 FR 96790/96830 (Dec 2024 FDP rules, HBM, 140 Entity List additions); 90 FR 4544 (Jan 2025, advanced computing and new AI model-weights control); 90 FR 47201 (Sep 2025 affiliates rule) and 90 FR 50857 ("stayed until November 9, 2026"); 90 FR 42321 (VEU revocation); 2026 BIS rule list (91 FR 1684 licence-policy change, UAE A:5, Cambodia D:5 removal, IC designer deadline, Entity List revisions; no new CCL semiconductor entries).
correction: Broadly supported, with two caveats: January 2025 also added a new item control (AI model weights, ECCN 4E091, via 90 FR 4544; informally rescinded May 2025 but still in the CFR), and the main 2025 end-user change, the 50% affiliates rule (90 FR 47201), was suspended from 10 Nov 2025 to 9 Nov 2026 (90 FR 50857). 2025-26 also loosened policy (H200 case-by-case review for China, UAE to A:5), not only adjusted lists.
notes: Interpretation; earlier stages (Huawei 2019-20, SMIC 2020, Oct 2022/2023) rely on existing claims and were not re-opened here.
